title: Infinite APN families from the general quadratic Fq2 template
summary: Determine whether the source-defined quadratic polynomial forms over a quadratic field extension yield a new infinite APN family.

formal_statement.body: For $q=2^m$, consider over $\mathbb F_{q^2}$ the narrower source form $$z^3+Az^{3q}+Bz^{2q+1}+Cz^{q+2}+Dz^5+Ez^{5q}+Fz^{4q+1}+Gz^{q+4}+Hz^{q+1}+Iz^{2(q+1)}$$ and the more general template $$\begin{aligned}f(z)={}&z(Az^2+Bz^4+Cz^q+Dz^{2q}+Ez^{4q})\\&+z^2(Gz^4+Hz^q+Iz^{2q}+Jz^{4q})\\&+z^4(Kz^q+Lz^{2q}+Mz^{4q})\\&+z^q(Nz^{2q}+Pz^{4q})+Qz^{6q}.\end{aligned}$$ Does either form produce a new infinite family of APN functions beyond the known families? Exhibit one coefficient choice valid for infinitely many admissible $m$ and prove its APN property and newness, or prove that no new infinite family occurs anywhere in the displayed forms.

scope.domain: Quadratic APN polynomial templates over $\mathbb F_{q^2}$
assumptions: The coefficients and exponents range over the complete template displayed in the source conclusion
Newness is assessed against the known APN families under the source equivalence conventions
parameters: coefficients in the two displayed source forms
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later work gives a conditional template extension and verifies finite instances, but its all-parameter construction depends on an unproved no-root conjecture. No unconditional new infinite family from the displayed source forms, and no global nonexistence theorem, was found.

citations.label: Li--Zhou--Li--Qu, general bivariate APN-template question
citations.locator: Conclusion and Further Work, journal pp. 4768--4769

progress.summary: The source asks whether its displayed general quadratic template over $\mathbb F_{q^2}$ yields new infinite APN families.
A later classification settles the strict $(q,q)$-biprojective subclass but does not give a new infinite-family witness for the broader source forms.
Later published work extends one source family and gives new finite instances, but its infinite construction depends on an unproved no-root conjecture.
